([[Northfield, Massachusetts]]) | college = * [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball|Western Kentucky]] (2018–2019) * [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]] (2020–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 46 | draft_team = [[Toronto Raptors]] | career_start = 2021 | years1 = {{nbay|2021|start}}–{{nbay|2022|end}} | team1 = [[Toronto Raptors]] | years2 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021]]–[[2022–23 NBA G League season|2023]] | team2 = →[[Raptors 905]] | years3 = {{nbay|2023|full=y}} | team3 = [[Boston Celtics]] | years4 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]] | team4 = →[[Maine Celtics]] | years5 = {{nbay|2023|end}}–{{nbay|2024|end}} | team5 = [[Portland Trail Blazers]] | years6 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–2026]] | team6 = [[Texas Legends]] | years7 = {{nbay|2025|end}} | team7 = [[Los Angeles Clippers]] | years8 = {{nbay|2025|end}} | team8 = Boston Celtics | highlights = }} '''Dalano Banton''' ({{IPAc-en|d|ə|ˈ|l|ɑː|n|oʊ|_|ˈ|b|æ|n|t|ən}} {{respell|də|LAH|noh|_|BAN|tən}};{{cite press release|title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2023|access-date=May 17, 2024}} born November 7, 1999) is a [[Canadians|Canadian]] professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Boston Celtics]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball|Western Kentucky Hilltoppers]] and [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska Cornhuskers]]. Banton was selected by the [[Toronto Raptors]] with the 46th overall pick in the [[2021 NBA draft]], making him the first Canadian player ever drafted by the Canadian franchise.{{Cite web |last=Loung |first=Steven |date=July 30, 2021 |title=Prospect of Interest: Raptors' first-ever Canadian selection Dalano Banton |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/prospect-interest-raptors-first-ever-canadian-selection-dalano-banton/ |access-date=October 18, 2025 |website=Sportsnet.ca}} ==Early life== Banton was born on November 7, 1999, in [[Toronto]], [[Ontario]], to a [[Jamaicans|Jamaican]] father and a [[Canadians|Canadian]] mother.{{cite web |last=Gheciu |first=Alex Nino |title='I Want to Be the Blueprint': The Raptors' Dalano Banton Is Making Rexdale Dream Big |url=https://www.complex.com/sports/a/alex-nino-gheciu/dalano-banton-toronto-raptors-feature |website=Complex |access-date=June 11, 2024 |date=October 21, 2021}} He grew up in the [[Smithfield, Toronto|Mount Olive]] area within the [[Rexdale]] neighborhood of Toronto. Banton began playing basketball as a child at the North Kipling Community Centre, the Rexdale Community Hub, and a local parking lot. He also attended basketball camps hosted by former [[Toronto Raptors|Toronto Raptor]] [[DeMar DeRozan]] in the neighborhood.{{Cite news |last=Ewing |first=Lori |date=September 29, 2021 |title=Rookie guard Dalano Banton living his dream with hometown Raptors |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/nba/nba-toronto-raptors-dalano-banton-1.6194443 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231204020005/https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/nba/nba-toronto-raptors-dalano-banton-1.6194443 |archive-date=Dec 4, 2023 |access-date=October 20, 2021 |work=[[CBC Sports]] |agency=[[The Canadian Press]]}} Banton, originally a member of 2019 class, [[reclassification (education)|reclassified]] into 2018. He played for Redemption Christian Academy in [[Northfield, Massachusetts]], and [[MacDuffie School]] in [[Granby, Massachusetts]].{{cite news |last=Stephens |first=Brad |title= Hilltoppers sign 4-Star Canada native Dalano Banton |url= https://www.bgdailynews.com/sports/wku/hilltoppers-sign-4-star-canada-native-dalano-banton/article_f60a04cb-022c-5b40-a4b5-c76d202cd21b.html |accessdate=January 1, 2021 |work=[[Bowling Green Daily News]] |date=November 14, 2017}} By the end of his high school career, Banton was a consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and was ranked in the top 100 recruits nationally in 2018 by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] (no. 80) and [[247Sports]] (no. 92). On November 14, 2017, Banton chose [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball|Western Kentucky]] over [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]], [[UMass Minutemen basketball|UMass]] and [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]]. {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2018}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Dalano Banton | position = G | hometown = [[Toronto, ON]] | highschool = Redemption Christian Academy (MA) | feet = 6 | inches = 7 | weight = 204 | 40 = | commitdate = November 14, 2017 | scout stars = 4 | rivals stars = 4 | 247 stars = 4 | espn stars = 0 | espn grade = NR }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2018 | rivals ref title = Western Kentucky 2018 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2018 Western Kentucky Hilltoppers Recruiting Class | rivals school = westernkentucky | scout s = | espn schoolid = 98 | 247 overall = 92 | rivals overall = 80 | espn overall = | accessdate = January 1, 2021 | bball = yes }} ==College career== As a freshman, Banton played 31 games at Western Kentucky, averaging 3.4 points, 3.0 rebounds and 2.1 assists per game. Banton made 12 starts and nearly had a [[triple-double]] with eight points, 13 rebounds and 10 assists in a career-high 38 minutes in a win over No. 15 [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]].{{cite magazine |title=Dalano Banton Helps Western Kentucky Beat No. 15 Wisconsin 83-76|url= https://www.si.com/college/2018/12/30/dalano-banton-western-kentucky-wisconsin |access-date=January 1, 2021 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=December 29, 2018}} Banton was one of only six players in [[NCAA Division I|Division I]] basketball to have a game with at least eight points, 13 rebounds and 10 assists in 2018–19. He had three double-figure scoring efforts on the season, including a season-high 11 points against both [[Belmont Bruins men's basketball|Belmont]] and [[Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball|Saint Mary's]], as he also had six assists and three blocks against the Gaels.{{cite web |title=Dalano Banton WKU Bio |url= https://wkusports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/dalano-banton/1682 |access-date=January 1, 2021 |work=WKU Sports |date=March 25, 2019}} On April 10, 2019, Banton announced his intent to transfer from Western Kentucky.{{cite news |last=Shircliffe |first=Ross |title= WKU Basketball: Dalano Banton to Transfer From Hill |url= https://medium.com/the-red-towel/wku-basketball-report-dalano-banton-to-transfer-from-hill-30345f720d06 |accessdate=January 1, 2021 |work=WKU Herald Sports |date=April 10, 2019}} On May 1, 2019, Banton announced, via Twitter, his commitment to Nebraska.{{cite news |last=Basnett |first=Chris |title= Huskers get commitment from 6-foot-8 transfer guard Banton |url= https://journalstar.com/sports/huskers/mens-basketball/huskers-get-commitment-from-6-foot-8-transfer-guard-banton/article_c8038433-cca5-554c-8c74-823594711d0a.html |accessdate=January 1, 2021 |work=[[Lincoln Journal Star]] |date=May 1, 2019}} Banton sat out the 2019–20 season after transferring from Western Kentucky and honed his skills on the scout team. Banton played during the Huskers' trip to Italy in August 2019, averaging 5.8 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.3 steals per game in helping the Huskers post a 4–0 record.{{cite web |title=Dalano Banton Nebraska Bio |url= https://huskers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/season/2020-21/player/dalano-banton |access-date=January 1, 2021 |work=Huskers.com |date=September 1, 2020}} On December 17, 2020, Banton recorded just the second triple-double in Nebraska men's basketball history with 13 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists in Nebraska's 110–64 win over [[Doane University]].{{cite news |last=Ward|first=Andrew|title= Banton records triple double, Husker Hoops routes Doane |url= https://www.klkntv.com/banton-records-triple-double-husker-hoops-routes-doane/|accessdate=January 1, 2021 |work=[[KLKN]] |date=December 17, 2020}} He averaged 9.6 points, 5.9 rebounds and 3.9 assists per game. Following the season, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite news |last=DuBose |first=Ben |title=Report: Nebraska prospect Dalano Banton to work out with Rockets |url=https://rocketswire.usatoday.com/2021/06/16/report-nebraska-prospect-dalano-banton-to-work-out-with-rockets/ |access-date=June 25, 2021 |work=Rockets Wire |date=June 16, 2021}} However, on July 2 he announced he was remaining in the draft.{{cite news |title=Dalano Banton Stays in 2021 NBA Draft |url=https://huskers.com/news/2021/07/02/dalano-banton-stays-in-2021-nba-draft |access-date=July 4, 2021 |work=Husker Athletics |date=July 2, 2021 |archive-date=July 3, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210703013210/https://huskers.com/news/2021/7/2/mens-basketball-dalano-banton-stays-in-2021-nba-draft.aspx |url-status=live }} ==Professional career== ===Toronto Raptors (2021–2023)=== Banton was drafted with the 46th overall pick in the [[2021 NBA draft]] by the [[Toronto Raptors]], making him the first-ever Canadian to be drafted by the franchise.{{cite news|first=Nick|last=Westoll|url=https://globalnews.ca/news/8075131/dalano-banton-toronto-raptors-nba-draft/|title=Toronto's Dalano Banton becomes 1st Canadian to be drafted by Raptors|work=Global News|date=July 30, 2020|accessdate=August 2, 2021}} On August 14, he signed a multi-year contract with the Raptors.{{cite web |last=Lopez |first=J. |date=August 14, 2021 |title=Raptors Sign Banton |url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/raptors-sign-banton |access-date=August 14, 2021 |website=NBA.com}} Banton chose to wear the number 45 to honour the [[Toronto Transit Commission|TTC]] 45 Kipling bus which regularly served the neighbourhood he grew up in. He made his professional debut on October 20, 2021, in the Raptors' season- and home-opener against the [[2021–22 Washington Wizards season|Washington Wizards]], and scored his first career points in the NBA with a [[buzzer]]-beating [[three-point field goal]] at the end of the third quarter.{{cite web |date=20 October 2021 |title=Raptors' Dalano Banton beats buzzer from half court to notch first career points |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/video/banton-beats-buzzer-half-court-notch-first-career-points/ |access-date=22 October 2021 |website=sportsnet.ca |archive-date=22 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211022132040/https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/video/banton-beats-buzzer-half-court-notch-first-career-points/ |url-status=dead }}{{cite news |title=Washington Wizards Toronto Raptors home opener |url=https://www.tsn.ca/washington-wizards-toronto-raptors-home-opener-1.1709274 |access-date=22 October 2021 |work=TSN.ca |agency=The Canadian Press |date=20 October 2021 |language=en |quote=Banton entered the game with 25 seconds left in the third in his NBA debut, and promptly knocked down a buzzer-beating three from 49 feet out to slice the Wizards' lead to 81-59 with one quarter to play.}} On November 13, Banton scored a season-high 12 points while adding three rebounds, two assists and a steal in a 127–121 loss to the [[2021–22 Detroit Pistons season|Detroit Pistons]]. On November 24, 2022, Banton scored a career-high 27 points, alongside four rebounds, four assists, three steals and two blocks, in a 115–111 win over the [[2022–23 Detroit Pistons season|Detroit Pistons]].{{Cite web |title=BANTON, BOUCHER LEAD SHORT-HANDED RAPTORS PAST PISTONS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200199 |access-date=February 1, 2023 |website=NBA.com|date=November 15, 2022|last=Hogg|first=Dave}} ===Boston Celtics (2023–2024)=== On July 3, 2023, Banton signed a two-year contract with the [[Boston Celtics]].{{Cite web |date=2023-07-03 |title=Report: Celtics signing guard Dalano Banton |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/boston/news/report-celtics-signing-guard-dalano-banton/ |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=cbsnews.com}} Banton made 24 appearances (including one start) for the Celtics during the [[2023–24 NBA season]], recording averages of 2.3 points, 1.5 rebounds, and 0.8 assists.{{Cite web|title=Dalano Banton 2023-24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4397885/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=July 27, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ===Portland Trail Blazers (2024–2025)=== On February 8, 2024, Banton was traded, along with cash, to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in exchange for a protected second-round pick.{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Acquire Dalano Banton From Celtics|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-acquire-dalano-banton-from-celtics|website=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 8, 2024}} On March 27, Banton scored a new career-high 31 points along with 5 rebounds and 9 assists in a 120–106 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web |last=Trocchi |first=Bill |date=March 27, 2024 |title=Dejounte Murray scores 30 points, Hawks hand Trail Blazers 8th straight loss with 120-106 victory |url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/basketball/dejounte-murray-scores-30-points-hawks-hand-trail-blazers-8th-straight-loss-with-120-106/article_9cdfa77c-3f43-51b8-8817-fdcdbd7ccc6c.html |access-date=March 28, 2024 |website=TheStar.com |agency=The Associated Press}} In Portland's season finale against the [[Sacramento Kings]] on April 14, Banton went 0-of-15 on shots beyond the arc. In doing so, he became the first player in NBA history to attempt as many three-point shots without a make.{{cite web |last=Rasmussen |first=Karl |date=April 15, 2024 |title=Trail Blazers' Dalano Banton Made Unwanted NBA History During Blowout Loss vs. Kings |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2024/04/14/trail-blazers-dalano-banton-unwanted-nba-history-three-pointers |access-date=April 16, 2024 |website=SI.com}} On November 4, 2024, Banton scored 20 points in under 12 minutes in a 118–100 victory over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]—the first time this feat had been performed in franchise history, as well as marking only the seventh instance of a player doing so across the NBA.{{Cite web |last=Moore |first=Joe |date=2024-11-04 |title=Dalano Banton Plays Hero Again as Blazers Beat Pelicans |url=https://www.blazersedge.com/2024/11/4/24288424/dalano-banton-portland-trail-blazers-new-orleans-pelicans-ayton-grant-brandon-ingram |access-date=2024-11-07 |website=Blazer's Edge |language=en}} ===Texas Legends (2025–2026)=== On October 7, 2025, the [[Dallas Mavericks]] signed Banton to an [[Exhibit 10]] contract. Just ten days later, on October 17, the Mavericks waived Banton, [[Dennis Smith Jr.]] and [[Jeremiah Robinson-Earl]].{{Cite web |last=Foglio |first=James |date=October 17, 2025 |title=Mavericks Release Dalano Banton, Jeremiah Robinson-Earl, Dennis Smith Jr. |url=https://www.basketballinsiders.org/news/mavericks-release-dalano-banton-jeremiah-robinson-earl-dennis-smith-jr/ |access-date=October 18, 2025 |website=Basketball Insiders}} He then signed with the Mavericks' G League affiliate, the [[Texas Legends]]. ===Los Angeles Clippers (2026)=== On February 8, 2026, Banton signed a ten-day contract with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{Cite web|date=February 7, 2026|title=Clippers' Dalano Banton: Gets 10-day deal with LAC|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/clippers-dalano-banton-gets-10-day-deal-with-lac/|access-date=February 7, 2026|website=CBS Sports}} In two appearances for the Clippers, Banton posted averages of 3.0 points, 0.5 rebounds, and 1.0 assists. Upon the expiration of the deal, he became a free agent.{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/dalano-banton-back-on-open-market/|title=Dalano Banton: Back on open market|date=February 17, 2026|website=CBS Sports}} === Second stint with Celtics (2026) === On February 19, 2026, Banton signed a ten-day contract to return to the [[Boston Celtics]].{{Cite web |last=Hartwell |first=Darren |date=2026-02-19 |title=Reunion in Boston: Celtics signing Dalano Banton to 10-day deal |url=https://www.nbcsportsboston.com/nba/boston-celtics/dalano-banton-10-day-contract/771203/ |access-date=2026-02-19 |website=NBC Sports Boston |language=en-US}} On April 11, the Celtics signed Banton to a two-year, standard contract.{{Cite web|title=Celtics Sign Dalano Banton|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/celtics-sign-dalano-banton|access-date=April 25, 2026|website=gleague.nba.com|language=en}} In four appearances for the team, he averaged 1.5 points, 1.0 rebounds, and 2.3 assists. On July 9, Banton was waived by the Celtics.{{Cite web|title=Dalano Banton: Waived by Boston|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/dalano-banton-waived-by-boston/|access-date=July 27, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== ====Regular season==== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2021}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2021–22 Toronto Raptors season|Toronto]] | 64 || 1 || 10.9 || .411 || .255 || .591 || 1.9 || 1.5 || .4 || .2 || 3.2 |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2022}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2022–23 Toronto Raptors season|Toronto]] | 31 || 2 || 9.0 || .423 || .294 || .708 || 1.5 || 1.2 || .4 || .4 || 4.6 |- | style="text-align:left;" rowspan=2|{{nbay|2023}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2023–24 Boston Celtics season|Boston]] | 24 || 1 || 7.1 || .373 || .125 || .800 || 1.5 || .8 || .2 || .1 || 2.3 |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2023–24 Portland Trail Blazers season|Portland]] | 30 || '''8''' || '''29.2''' || .408 || .311 || .780 || '''4.8''' || '''3.6''' || '''.9''' || .6 || '''16.7''' |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2024}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2024–25 Portland Trail Blazers season|Portland]] | '''67''' || 7 || 16.7 || .391 || '''.324''' || .728 || 2.0 || 2.4 || .6 || .5 || 8.3 |- | style="text-align:left;" rowspan=2|{{nbay|2025}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2025–26 Los Angeles Clippers season|L.A.
